create.name: Ashtanga Nilayam Singapore
create.bio:
Ashtanga Nilayam is a traditional Ashtanga shala on Race Course Road in Singapore, a short walk from Little India. Marta Magdalena and John Tattva opened it in 2019 after meeting in Mysore two years earlier; both hold Level 2 authorisation from the Sharath Yoga Centre. Marta had run her own Ashtanga shala in Berlin from 2014 and gives particular weight to pranayama, Ayurveda and the study of Vedic chanting, while John began teaching in New Delhi in 2012 and has taught in Singapore since 2016. Nilayam is a Sanskrit word for a dwelling or place of rest.

The heart of the school is the daily Mysore programme, in which each student learns the sequence step by step with individual help, so newcomers need no prior knowledge of the series; weekly led classes, one-to-one sessions, kids' yoga and a monthly community class run alongside. Beginners can start with a short Introduction to Ashtanga course covering sun salutations, the tristhana method of breath, posture and gaze, and the standing postures. The founders also teach a hatha-based pranayama and kriya workshop drawing on the Hatha Yoga Pradipika, run a second Mysore morning in Joo Chiat with a partner studio, and lead group trips, including one to Mysore and Bengaluru.

courses.title: Mysore class packages and Sadhana memberships
courses.description: Class packs, unlimited months and year-long Sadhana memberships for the shala's Mysore and led classes, plus reduced trial packs for new students living in Singapore. Drop-in visitors are welcome.
courses.price: Unlimited Sadhana $330/month and Mini Sadhana $299/month (1-year contracts); 1 Month Unlimited $360; 10 Classes $350; 1 Class Drop-In $50

courses.title: Daily Mysore programme
courses.description: Morning and evening Mysore-style sessions in which students learn the Ashtanga series gradually, guided one by one by the teacher. Beginners are encouraged to start here, with a choice of trial packs.

courses.title: Intro To Ashtanga workshop
courses.description: A beginners' course run either as one three-hour Sunday session or as four Wednesday evenings. It covers sun salutations, the tristhana method, the standing postures and their names, and how to set up a self-practice, and includes two weeks of unlimited classes.
courses.price: 169$ (Sunday format) or 199$ (four Wednesdays), each including a 2-week unlimited pass

courses.title: Pranayama Workshop
courses.description: A workshop on the bandhas, the classical cleansing kriyas and the pranayama techniques described in the Hatha Yoga Pradipika, from alternate-nostril breathing to bhastrika. Participants take home a short daily breathing sequence.

The site is on Wix, so its photos (static.wixstatic.com) can't be used; the only image is the shala's YouTube channel avatar, a Nilayam logo (yt3.ggpht.com, looked at). Owner may prefer a studio photo if one can be supplied.
Prices are published with '$' (Singapore context; the Ashtanga Essentials page uses SGD); written as published, no code added.
Pranayama workshop page lists physiological benefits (lung capacity, cardiovascular support); none repeated in the description. Kept as a classical pranayama and kriya workshop; drop if borderline.
Videos are short promotional montages of the shala and its Bali retreats (2:45–4:03); thin as teaching content.
Possible future listings: Marta Magdalena Glowacka, John Tattva (John Jinson).
